title: Descent of coherent Verdier duality and evaluation before retract restriction
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l different from its characteristic, an algebraic closure Omega of Q_l in an independent universe, and a separated finite-type D.k-scheme X. Use the raw finite rational categories and the actual common-stage category of [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data]. There exists DualityData B with the following core equations: its finite beta maps are coherent for the actual unit and associator; its dual is additive and Omega-linear; the Omega action on included finite maps is the specified coefficient embedding; its dual retains the literal original coefficient stage and its inclusion comparison has identity components; the scalar comparison square and evaluation-defined biduality descent hold; its omega comparisons commute with the finite dualizing u maps; its evaluation is the included finite evaluation through the canonical tensor comparison and duality comparison; and evaluation is natural in its contravariant argument. These are CoreProperties. For any such B, the three additional split-retract formulas of DualityProperties follow, so B canonically completes to a Duality.

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal C_E(W)=D^b_c(W,E)$ for the rationalized stages used in the statement and $T_{M/E}$ for their scalar extension. Form the pair category from these stages exactly as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. We construct the contravariant functor directly on its representatives. By [thm-coef-rational-verdier], $D_E=D_{W,E}$ is a contravariant exact $E$-linear equivalence, with coherent isomorphisms $b_{M/E,K}:T_{M/E}D_EK\to D_M(T_{M/E}K)$. Define $D(E,K)=(E,D_EK)$ and, for $u:T_{M/E}K\to T_{M/F}L$, put
$$d_M(u)=b_{M/E,K}^{-1}\circ D_M(u)\circ b_{M/F,L}:
T_{M/F}D_FL\longrightarrow T_{M/E}D_EK.$$
This has exactly the source and target required for a representative of $D(F,L)\to D(E,K)$.

Choose the finite rational internal-Hom identifications and use the normalized simultaneous scalar comparisons. Their integral unit and tower formulas fix the same finite beta maps, including repeated coefficient fields.

Use the opposite-stage equivalence and coherent pair-functor descent to descend the contravariant representative formula. The resulting object formula retains the literal stage and gives identity inclusion comparisons.

Use intrinsicQbarLinear on the already specified common-stage category. Its finite-representative scalar formula gives the coefficient embedding normalization; at a common extension containing the scalar, finite linearity gives Omega-linearity of the dual. Represent a distinguished triangle at a finite stage; the evaluation-defined finite shift comparisons commute with scalar extension by uniqueness of their tensor-Hom transposes. They descend and carry the triangle to the distinguished finite dual triangle.

Represent omega at the base coefficient stage. The finite canonical u maps identify this with every finite omega. Descend finite evaluation and biduality using their scalar squares and the actual common-stage tensor object formula. The finite inverse biduality map descends too and proves invertibility and the anti-equivalence. Their finite equations give all scalar, omega and evaluation normalizations and evaluation naturality.

For a split pair i:P to K and p:K to P, factor tensor(i,Dp) as tensor(i,1) followed by tensor(1,Dp), and use evaluation naturality for p. Functoriality and i followed by p equal identity give evaluation at P. Naturality of the bidual isomorphism and its inverse gives the other two retract equations. Thus the core completes to the full unchanged DualityProperties.
